why: The output avoids both must_not items. For item 1, the README expect line says "Every function exported by index.js has its own `## name(` heading... capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft". Its run proof compares the README headings against the exports with deepEqual. A build that adds only a padLeft section and leaves slugify undocumented would fail this check. The separate padLeft-section line is an extra check, not a substitute for it. For item 2, every padLeft expect line checks what the function returns, such as padLeft('42',5,'0') giving '00042', number input, space default and no truncation. None of them says how padLeft must be built. padStart appears only once, under assumptions, where "modelled on String.prototype.padStart" describes the signature. It is not an expect line and does not require padStart to be used.
